clue.text: Terrible commotion behind us

parts.note: behind is a colloquial word for the rump or backside

explanation.surface: Someone complains of a dreadful racket going on at their back.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumpus is a noisy disturbance or uproar, a fair match for a terrible commotion.

clue.text: Britain's announced decree

indicators.note: announced means the letters for the country's possessive are spoken aloud

parts.note: Britain is the UK, so Britain's is UK'S

explanation.surface: A news item reports a proclamation issued by the British state.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, UK'S (you-kays) sounds like the word for a Russian imperial edict.
explanation.definitionFit: A ukase was an edict of the Russian tsar, and by extension any arbitrary order.

clue.text: Help gran in struggle to catch a wild creature

indicators.note: to catch says the rearranged letters close around the single letter a
in struggle suggests the letters of help and gran are tossed about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A plea to assist grandma as she tries to trap an animal on the loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in struggle' rearranges HELPGRAN into PHLANGER, and 'to catch' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phalanger is an Australasian marsupial such as a possum, an animal living in the wild.

clue.text: During breaks companion provided drink

indicators.note: During says the companion's letters come in the middle of the word for breaks

parts.note: breaks, as a twig does, means snaps
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A friend offered a beverage in the course of work breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Schnapps is a strong spirit, so a type of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Film director is against appearing in ITV retrospective

indicators.note: appearing in places the other pieces within the turned-round channel
retrospective means looking back, so the letters of the channel are read from the end

parts.note: con is the case against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: A film-maker objects to being featured in a television channel's look back at his career.
explanation.walkthrough: ITV is a British commercial television network; 'against' gives CON, as in pros and cons.
explanation.definitionFit: Luchino Visconti was an Italian filmmaker who directed The Leopard and Death in Venice.

clue.text: Journey's end for some in visit to Croatian resort

indicators.note: resort is read as re-sort, so the letters of the preceding words are sorted again

explanation.surface: A holiday visit takes some people to a seaside town on the Adriatic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday destination but signals re-sorting the letters of VISIT TO CROATIAN. VICTORIA STATION is a major London rail terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: A rail terminus is where trains finish their run, so passengers arriving there end their trip.

clue.text: Went off course, ready to regroup beyond street

indicators.note: beyond says the rearranged letters lie further on than the abbreviation for street
to regroup means the letters of ready are gathered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wandered off the route, preparing to rally the troops further along the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beyond' tells you the rearranged letters come after the street abbreviation, not before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To stray is to wander from the proper path or route.

clue.text: Attack in centre of Durham town

indicators.note: centre of means only the inside letters of the town's name are kept, dropping the first and last

parts.note: Consett is a former steel town in County Durham

explanation.surface: An assault takes place in the middle of a town in north-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: Consett is a town in County Durham, in north-east England; losing its first and last letters leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is an assault or first rush against an enemy.

clue.text: End of story still to be heard

indicators.note: to be heard says the words for story and still are spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a story is a tale and stillness is peace

explanation.surface: A listener waits for the conclusion of a narrative that has not yet been told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End' alone is the definition; 'of' is a link, and the surface's 'End of story' is a false phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailpiece is a final section or appendage added at the close of something.

clue.text: Writer secured copyright in new version of Hair, a stage hit

indicators.note: secured says the rearranged letters hold the copyright symbol within them
new version of says the letters of the musical's description are rearranged

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for copyright, as in the circled C symbol

explanation.surface: An author protects her rights on a fresh adaptation of the musical Hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new version of' rearranges HAIRASTAGEHIT, and 'secured' tucks C inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie was the English crime novelist who created Poirot and Miss Marple.

clue.text: Putting things right in one kind of school after head's dismissed

indicators.note: after head's dismissed means the first letter of the school word is removed

parts.note: a preparatory school prepares young pupils for a later school

explanation.surface: Things are being sorted out at a school once the headteacher has been sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: A PREPARATORY (prep) school is a British private school for younger children; dropping its first letter gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Reparatory describes making amends or repairs, setting matters back in order.

clue.text: Mistake printed in copy that's sent back

indicators.note: sent back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An error has appeared in a document, so it is returned to the writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points into COPY THAT'S, where OPYT sits; 'sent back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A typographical error is a slip made in typing or typesetting text.

clue.text: Food unpleasant old woman served to soldiers

parts.note: a hag is an ugly or spiteful old woman
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: A nasty old woman dishes up meals to the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: HAGGIS is a Scottish dish of sheep's offal and oatmeal cooked in a casing.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggis is a traditional Scottish pudding, a dish for eating.

clue.text: Rain came unexpectedly, drowning a group from New York?

indicators.note: drowning says the rearranged letters cover and surround the letter a
unexpectedly suggests the letters of rain and came fall into a surprising order

explanation.surface: A sudden downpour swamps a band from New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' rearranges RAINCAME into AMERICAN, and 'drowning' swallows A. The question mark marks the definition as an example: New York items are one source of American artefacts.
explanation.definitionFit: Americana is a collection of things typical of the United States, of which New York is one part.

clue.text: Trendy young woman and man owing money

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
a deb is a debutante, a young woman entering society
Ted is a man's name

explanation.surface: A fashionable debutante and her boyfriend are in debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in debt means a sum is owed to a lender.

clue.text: Before every formal dance book a bouncer?

indicators.note: Before says the abbreviation for book goes ahead of the other two pieces

parts.note: each means every
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A social secretary reserves a doorman ahead of each grand dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bouncer?' looks like a nightclub doorman, but is something that bounces on the sand.
explanation.definitionFit: A large inflatable toy for the seaside bounces readily when thrown or kicked.

clue.text: Produces new piece about western customs

parts.note: re means about or concerning
rites are ceremonial customs

explanation.surface: A writer turns out a fresh article on the traditions of the West.
explanation.definitionFit: To redraft a text is to create a new version of a piece of writing.

clue.text: Advice given to minor (though not unknown) composer

parts.note: a tip is a piece of advice

indicators.note: not unknown says a mathematical unknown, the letter y, is removed

parts.note: petty means minor or trivial

explanation.surface: Guidance offered to a lesser-known composer of no great fame.
explanation.walkthrough: Y is one of the algebra letters (x, y, z) standing for an unknown. Michael Tippett was an English composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Michael Tippett wrote the oratorio A Child of Our Time and several operas.

clue.text: One forking out about a pound for gramophone

indicators.note: about says the payer's letters go round the pound sign

parts.note: forking out is slang for paying, so this is a payer
L stands for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone shells out about a pound for an old record machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A record player is the modern name for a gramophone, which plays discs.

clue.text: Removes carpets

definitions.meaning: removes, as weeds or floorboards are lifted out
carpets as a verb, meaning reprimands or tells off

explanation.surface: A workman takes up the rugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull up is to uproot something, and also to rebuke someone for a fault.

clue.text: Dismiss strong criticism

definitions.meaning: dismiss means sack from a job
strong criticism, as in coming under heavy attack

explanation.surface: A boss sends someone packing after harsh complaints.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack someone is to let them go, and a barrage of censure is described as coming under it.

clue.text: Drunk topes in bar legally

indicators.note: Drunk suggests the letters of topes stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker is in a pub, behaving lawfully.
explanation.walkthrough: To tope is to drink heavily, so 'topes' and 'Drunk' and 'bar' build a pub scene; the bar is a legal one.
explanation.definitionFit: Estop is a legal term meaning to preclude or prevent someone from asserting something.

clue.text: Pale old actress

definitions.meaning: pale means light in colour, like a creamy off-white
an actress of the silent-film era, star of The Perils of Pauline

explanation.surface: A veteran performer looks wan.
explanation.definitionFit: The shade of nacre is a soft lustrous white, and the silent serial star of that name worked in early cinema.

clue.text: Set of verb forms used in written sentences

indicators.note: used in says the answer is found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Grammar notes on which verb conjugations appear in written prose.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical tense is a set of verb forms showing the time of an action.

clue.text: Players should have less trouble with home fixture? Some hopes!

definitions.text: Players should have less trouble with home fixture?
definitions.meaning: a whimsical reading: Spanish teams playing in their own grounds, with home grounds pictured as fortresses
an exclamation of scorn at an unrealistic dream

explanation.surface: A sports pundit predicts an easy home win, then scoffs at the idea.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means daydreams or impossible schemes; the first reading pictures home sides in Spain playing in their own fortresses.
explanation.definitionFit: Visionary projects with no chance of coming true are fanciful dreams, mocked by 'Some hopes!'

clue.text: Evil character from capital of Russia, not unlike recent Russian leader

indicators.note: capital of means the first letter of the following word

parts.note: as means like, so not unlike is as
Vladimir Putin, the Russian president

explanation.surface: A sinister figure from Moscow bears a resemblance to a recent Kremlin boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital of Russia' looks like Moscow but means its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Grigori Rasputin was the notorious mystic at the court of the last tsar, remembered as a villain.

clue.text: Window decoration is dear, with wood inlay

indicators.note: inlay says the wood is set into the word for dear

parts.note: pet is a term of endearment, like dear
elm is a kind of wood

explanation.surface: A curtain fitting is costly because of its timber inlay.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelmet is a narrow border fitted above a window to conceal the curtain rail.
